chunks: And whatever is in it from Ali ibn Maṭar, I have narrated it from Ahmad ibn Ziyad ibn Jafar Al-Hamadani - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ali ibn Maṭar.

key_terms.أَحْمَدُ بْنُ زِيَادِ: Ahmad ibn Ziyad, a key link in the transmission chain.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a honorific used for companions or scholars.
key_terms.عَلِيٌّ بْنُ مَطَرٍ: Ali ibn Maṭar, a narrator whose reports are being authenticated.
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, another narrator in the chain.

ai.seo_question: How is the transmission chain for Ali ibn Maṭar's narrations verified in Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq clarifies the specific isnad for narrations of Ali ibn Maṭar, noting that while some reports in the book are from him, this particular chain was transmitted via Ahmad ibn Ziyad al-Hamdani. This biographical precision underscores the rigorous standards of hadith verification in Shia scholarship, ensuring the reliability of the Imam's teachings by tracing them through a distinct and verified lineage of narrators.
